entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that despite having consensual relation of the complainant with the petitioner, she has falsely implicated the petitioner by lodging FIR on 21.08.2021 for the incident of 2017 without explaining delay properly.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has shown some photographs of the petitioner and the complainant to submit that they were happily enjoying their life and she had no grievance against the petitioner.

He has further submitted that as a matter of fact, the complainant was trying to blackmail the petitioner demanding money and the petitioner has provided some money to her but when he could not satisfy her undue demands, she lodged an FIR.
The impugned FIR and its charge sheet is nothing but misuse of the process of the law, therefore, the charge sheet may be quashed.

5. Per contra, Sri Aniruddh Kumar Singh, learned AGA-I, has stated that in the present case, serious allegations have been levelled against the petitioner and after completion of investigation, the charge sheet has been filed under those serious Sections.

Not only the above, statements of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C. are intact, therefore, the entire proceedings emanating from Crime No.057 of 2021, under Sections 201, 328, 376, 377, 420, IPC and Section 66 E of the I.T. Act, 2008 may not be set aside/ quashed by invoking the powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
6.

Be that as it may, after hearing learned counsel for the parties and perusing the material available on record, I do not find any convincing ground to invoke power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. quashing the charge sheet and further criminal proceedings emanating from Crime No.057 of 2021 (supra),
therefore, the present petition is dismissed.

7. However, it is always open for the petitioner to avail appropriate remedy before the appropriate court of law at various stages and it is needless to say that if the present petitioner adopts any legal recourse before the appropriate court of law at appropriate stages, the same may be considered and decided strictly in accordance with law and in that case, application of mind of the court concerned should be reflected.
[Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.] Order Date :- 17.1.2024 RBS/-
